user.title: Add a HomeKit accessory
user.description: Each accessory is added to Apple Home on its own with its own pairing code, or into one of your HomeKit Bridges.

menu_option_descriptions.irrigation: Valves become the zones of one Irrigation System. Each zone has its own run time and closes by itself; turning the system on runs every zone in turn.
menu_option_descriptions.ceiling_fan: A fan and its light as one accessory, instead of two separate tiles.
menu_option_descriptions.buttons: Event entities become HomeKit buttons with single, double and long press, ready for Home automations.
menu_option_descriptions.multi_sensor: Motion, contact, leak, temperature, humidity, light level and battery from one device as one accessory.
menu_option_descriptions.air_quality: All pollutant readings on one Air Quality sensor, rated by the worst one.
menu_option_descriptions.air_purifier: A fan plus optional air quality, humidity, temperature and filter sensors as one Air Purifier.
menu_option_descriptions.power_strip: Several switches as the numbered outlets of one accessory.
menu_option_descriptions.faucet: Valves become the outlets of one Shower or Faucet. Turning it on opens them all.

run_times.title: Run times for {name}
run_times.description:
How long each zone runs when started from Apple Home, in seconds. Run times changed in Apple Home are saved too.

{details}

duplicates.title: Already in {bridge}
duplicates.description:
{bridge} also publishes {entities} as separate accessories, so they would show up twice in Apple Home.

To avoid that, open the HomeKit Bridge integration's options for {bridge} and exclude them. You can continue now and do that afterwards.

entities.title: Choose entities for {name}
entities.description: Anything found on the device you picked is already filled in. Adjust as needed.

data.use_controller_timers: Use the controller's run times and countdown

data_description.valves: Each valve becomes a zone (or outlet), named after the valve.
data_description.default_duration: Starting run time for each zone; you can set each zone's own run time on the next step. Up to 3600 seconds; 0 runs until stopped.
data_description.valve_type: How Apple Home shows each outlet.
data_description.one_at_a_time: Starting a zone stops the one that's running. Turning the whole system on always runs zones one after another.
data_description.use_controller_timers: When a valve's device also has a run-time number and a time-remaining sensor (Rain Bird Extended, for example), Apple Home's run time and countdown use them and the controller ends each run.
data_description.separate_zones: Publish each zone as a numbered valve instead of zones inside an Irrigation System. It's still one accessory, and Apple Home offers to show each valve as its own tile (accessory settings → Show as Separate Tiles), so zones can go in different rooms. There's no system switch to run every zone in turn.
data_description.master: Optional. Turned on while any zone runs and off 5 seconds after the last one stops. It isn't added to Apple Home.
data_description.events: Each event entity becomes one button, or one per physical button if it covers a whole remote (button_1_single, button_2_hold, ...). Single, double and long presses are recognized from the event types the device reports.
data_description.aqi_sensor: If set, this decides the overall rating instead of the individual pollutants.
data_description.co2_sensor: In ppm. Also shown as a Carbon Dioxide sensor that alerts at 1000 ppm.
data_description.air_quality_sensor: A HomeKit 1-5 value or an AQI value.
data_description.filter_life_sensor: Remaining filter life in %. Apple Home asks for a replacement at 10% or less.
data_description.battery_sensor: Apple Home warns at 20% or less.
data_description.outlets: Switches or input booleans, in outlet order.
data_description.fan: Speed, oscillation and direction are added when the fan supports them.
data_description.light: Brightness is added when the light supports it.

accessory_info.name: Accessory information
accessory_info.description: What Apple Home shows under the accessory's details. Leave fields empty to use the details of the device you picked, or of the device the entities belong to.

data_description.manufacturer: Leave empty to use the device's manufacturer.
data_description.model: Leave empty to use the device's model.
data_description.serial_number: Leave empty to use the device's serial number or MAC address. At least 2 characters.
data_description.firmware: Numbers only: 1, 1.2 or 1.2.3. Leave empty to use the device's firmware version.

irrigation.title: Irrigation system
irrigation.description:
Valves become the zones of one Irrigation System. Each zone has its own run time and closes by itself; turning the system on runs every zone in turn.

Pick the device it represents to fill in its entities for you, or leave it empty to choose entities yourself.

data_description.name: Shown in Apple Home. Defaults to the device's name.
data_description.device: Optional. Its matching entities are selected on the next step.
data_description.bridge: Standalone accessories have their own pairing code. Adding to one of your HomeKit Bridges puts the accessory in a bridge already paired with Apple Home, so there's nothing more to pair.

connection.name: Connection
connection.description: For standalone accessories. Usually fine as suggested.

data_description.port: Each accessory needs its own port. A free one is suggested.
data_description.pin: 8 digits as 123-45-678. A random code is suggested.
data_description.plain_name: Show just the name ("Irrigation System") when Apple Home and Home Assistant discover the accessory, instead of the name plus part of its ID ("Irrigation System 8D111D"). Falls back to the ID suffix if another device already uses the name.

error.invalid_pin: Use the format 123-45-678. HomeKit doesn't allow repeated digits, 123-45-678 or 876-54-321.
error.port_in_use: Another HomeKit accessory or bridge in Home Assistant is set up to use this port.
error.port_busy: Something else on this host is already using this port, such as the old HomeKit Irrigation or Air Purifier integration. Pick another port or stop that service.
error.serial_too_short: Use at least 2 characters, or leave it empty.
error.invalid_firmware: HomeKit only accepts versions like 1, 1.2 or 1.2.3.
error.bridge_missing: That HomeKit Bridge no longer exists or isn't in bridge mode. Pick another, or Standalone.
error.master_is_zone: The pump or master valve can't also be a zone.
error.no_buttons_selected: Select at least one event entity.
error.no_sensors_selected: Select at least one sensor besides the battery.
error.no_pollutants_selected: Select an air quality index or at least one pollutant sensor.

run_times.description:
How long each zone runs when started from Apple Home, in seconds. Changes apply right away without re-pairing.

{details}

info.title: Accessory information for {name}
info.description:
What Apple Home shows under the accessory's details. Empty fields come from the device this accessory represents, or from HomeKit Extended if the device doesn't say. Right now that's: {defaults}.

Changes apply right away. "HomeKit Certified" can't be changed; it's only Yes for devices certified by Apple.

data_description.manufacturer: Leave empty to use the device's manufacturer.
data_description.model: Leave empty to use the device's model.
data_description.serial_number: Leave empty to use the device's serial number or MAC address. At least 2 characters.
data_description.firmware: Numbers only: 1, 1.2 or 1.2.3. Leave empty to use the device's firmware version.

connection.title: Bridge, port and pairing code
connection.description: Changes take effect right away. The port and pairing code only apply to standalone accessories, and a new pairing code only matters when pairing again. Moving an accessory into or out of a bridge adds it to Apple Home as a new accessory, so rooms and automations need setting up again.

data_description.bridge: Standalone accessories have their own pairing code. Adding to one of your HomeKit Bridges puts the accessory in a bridge already paired with Apple Home, so there's nothing more to pair.
data_description.port: Each accessory needs its own port. A free one is suggested.
data_description.pin: 8 digits as 123-45-678. A random code is suggested.
data_description.plain_name: Show just the name ("Irrigation System") when Apple Home and Home Assistant discover the accessory, instead of the name plus part of its ID ("Irrigation System 8D111D"). Falls back to the ID suffix if another device already uses the name.

data_description.reset_pairing: Forgets every Apple Home pairing so the accessory can be added again. Remove it from Apple Home first.

options.standalone: Standalone, with its own pairing code

bridge_missing.title: {name} has no HomeKit Bridge
bridge_missing.description:
{name} was added to a HomeKit Bridge that has been deleted, disabled or switched to accessory mode, so it isn't in Apple Home right now. If you enable the bridge again or switch it back to bridge mode, {name} rejoins it by itself.

Open HomeKit Extended, choose **Configure** on {name}, then **Bridge, port and pairing code** to pick another bridge or publish it standalone.

bridge_unsupported.title: {name} can't join a HomeKit Bridge in this version of Home Assistant
bridge_unsupported.description: This version of Home Assistant's HomeKit Bridge works differently from what HomeKit Extended expects, so {name} can't be added to a bridge. Update HomeKit Extended, or open its options and publish {name} standalone for now.

bridge_full.title: {bridge} is full
bridge_full.description: HomeKit allows 150 accessories per bridge, and {bridge} already has that many, so {name} wasn't added. Exclude some entities from {bridge}, or publish {name} standalone.

duplicate_entities.title: {name} duplicates accessories in {bridge}
duplicate_entities.description: {bridge} also publishes {entities} as separate accessories, so they show up twice in Apple Home. Open the HomeKit Bridge integration's options for {bridge} and exclude them.
